searchText: We could decrease the block gas limit over time as well. That one is pretty simple and I think would have the desired effect of making the chain less and less useful. Couldn't a decreasing block gas limit be counteracted by the gas limit voting algorithm? <@755590043632140352> I don't think any transactions would have to be the reincluded in the approach of disabling slots. It would just be a slot that no validator is assigned to. So the execution client doesn't even produce any block for that slot. My idea above to artificially delay finalization doesn't work. Casper is robust, it doesn't matter if one doesn't call it finalized, nothing will revert from a justified epoch whose child is justified. I thought at first that this would be very hard to implement, but I think now that it may not be that bad. We may even have an artificial list of invalid indices that are added to the current shuffling algo and grow that list over time Not going to argue this point, but I'm against continuing the ice age after the merge. If there is a failure to reach reasonable social consensus on a specific upgrade, or upgrades in general, there may be a good reason for it. Creating a forcing function removes the ability to ask the question "do we need to upgrade?", which to me appears to be a reduction in freedom. Meta-question: what would be the proper platform to discuss the general pros and cons of an ice age? This goes very much into the governance discussion direction, which seems to be discouraged here on the discord server. Maybe we need a governance server or section 🙂 ethresearch discourages governance too Status quo is governance discussions only happen on calls? double standard? I think ethereum-magicians is a good place for this?
